title: Author uploads, replaces, unpublishes and deletes HTML reports from the admin pages
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The admin page offers an upload form for one .html file with title, slug and a publish-now-or-draft choice (derived from 'From the admin page the author uploads ... gives it a title and slug, and publishes it now or saves it as a draft'): missing
The owner uploads a single self-contained .html file under a title and slug, and it is stored as a report (row plus file under the data dir): missing
Only one .html file is accepted. Other files and bad fields are refused and leave nothing behind (derived from 'a single self-contained .html file' and 'gives it a title and slug'): missing
Publish now sets the report published with a date; save as draft leaves it unpublished: missing

Replacing a report: uploading again under the same slug swaps the bytes and title and keeps the report's identity (id and original publish date), so later likes and comments stay attached (from merged SC-003): missing
Unpublish a report (and republish it, keeping the original date): missing
Delete a report: its record and its file are both removed: missing
Every report admin page and action is reachable only by the pinned owner, and cross-origin POSTs are refused: missing

The old-gone and old-unreadable exits of recoverSetAside cannot be planted portably (a race, and permissions or a sharing violation). They are listed with reasons under unplantable_exits in the corpus, not exercised by a row.

deviation: Open now fails when a set-aside file cannot be restored or judged, in addition to keeping it. The review offered this as the alternative: a held-open or blocked file in place means the row and the served bytes disagree (ETag and size from v1, bytes v2). Fail closed, with the file named in the error and kept for the next start. The cost is that a stuck recovery blocks startup until a person clears the blocking file.
deviation: A directory or other non-regular file named tmp/<id>.old is treated as junk and swept, not kept and not an error. We never create one, and it holds no bytes to lose.

drift: internal/server/templates/admin_report.html:25-27 renders Unpublish when the report is published and Publish otherwise, not both. The design's edit page 'has publish, unpublish and delete forms', and the build did not declare this. The finish-line POSTs go to the action URLs directly, so they are unaffected. Carried from the first pass; still true of the tree.

attempts.summary: O-002 and O-003 are one defect and one fix.

caused_by.reason: 2 defect(s) in lines this slice wrote were accepted by the code review (O-002, O-003). None weighs a lap on its own, so they go back to the builder TOGETHER, once, before validation -- instead of to the backlog and from there to a send-back at the merge. Fix exactly these with the smallest change: one scoped re-check reads only your fix. Sent back with what raised them: O-002 (fix): m1 (minor): Open's sweep calls recoverSetAside for each tmp/<id>.old and then unconditionally RemoveAll's every tmp entry. recoverSetAside has two failure paths: the row lookup errors with something other than no-rows ('no row (or unreadable)'), or os.Rename(old, cur) fails, where it logs 'could not restore a set-aside file' and returns. Either way the sweep then deletes tmp/<id>.old, which in that state is the only copy of the bytes the row describes. The report's bytes are lost for good, and from then on the file in place no longer matches the row's sha256 and size: the ETag and the size advertise v1 while v2 is served. This contradicts the comment at lines 159-160, the declared m10 deviation ('a crash mid-replace must not delete the only copy'), and replace()'s restore-failure log 'the next start recovers it' (upload.go:384), which only holds if that next start's rename succeeds. Measured on this PC with an overlay probe: the file in place was held open, Open logged 'rename ...tmp\1.old ...reports\1.html: Access is denied.', and tmp/ was then empty with reports/1.html still v2. Have recoverSetAside return whether the .old must be kept: true when the rename back fails, and true when the row lookup fails with an error other than sql.ErrNoRows. The sweep should then skip RemoveAll for those names. Alternatively, return an error from Open so the server does not start serving a file that does not match its row. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. m1 is one member of "set-aside recovery failure paths that fall through to clearing tmp/" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-002/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close. Bound the class by who produces its members, not by every exotic spelling. Answer this obligation with `corpus`: the corpus's path from the repository root. It is not discharged without one. [shown by a failing run] The engine ran the code review's test for this, internal/reports/sweep_restore_failure_test.go, with `go test -count=1 -run ^TestOpenKeepsTheOnlyCopyWhenRestoreFails$ ./internal/reports`, and it FAILED. Put that test at internal/reports/sweep_restore_failure_test.go as it is -- comments and layout aside -- and make it pass. The engine runs `go test -count=1 -run ^TestOpenKeepsTheOnlyCopyWhenRestoreFails$ ./internal/reports` again in your tree, and that run is what closes this; your word does not. The test: package reports import ( "bytes" "os" "runtime" "testing" ) // m10: when a restart finds tmp/<id>.old holding the bytes the row describes // but cannot put it back (here: the file in place is held open, so Windows // refuses the rename), the sweep must not then delete that set-aside file. It // is the only copy of the report the row describes. func TestOpenKeepsTheOnlyCopyWhenRestoreFails(t *testing.T) { if runtime.GOOS != "windows" { t.Skip("holding the target open makes the rename fail only on Windows") } r := newRig(t) v1, v2 := htmlOf(300, "v1"), htmlOf(400, "v2") rep := r.mustSave(goodForm("crash", "Crash", "published", v1)) // A crash after the new file was renamed in but before the commit: the row // still describes v1, v1 is set aside, v2 is in place. must(t, os.WriteFile(r.lib.setAsidePath(rep.ID), v1, 0o600)) must(t, os.WriteFile(r.lib.path(rep.ID), v2, 0o600)) held, err := os.Open(r.lib.path(rep.ID)) if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } _, _ = Open(Options{DB: r.st.DB(), DataDir: r.root, MaxUploadBytes: testCap, Now: r.clock.Now}) held.Close() cur, _ := os.ReadFile(r.lib.path(rep.ID)) old, _ := os.ReadFile(r.lib.setAsidePath(rep.ID)) if !bytes.Equal(cur, v1) && !bytes.Equal(old, v1) { t.Fatal("the sweep deleted tmp/<id>.old after failing to restore it: the bytes the row describes are gone") } } O-003 (fix): IN-m1 (minor): The sweep deletes the only copy of a report's bytes when it fails to restore it. A replace interrupted after setAside leaves the row's bytes only in tmp/<id>.old. recoverSetAside (lines 201-220) returns silently in two cases: when its row lookup errors (line 203-204, any error, not only ErrNoRows), and when the restoring os.Rename fails (line 215-218, which only logs). In both cases the second loop (lines 167-171) RemoveAll's every tmp entry, that .old included. The row survives with no file behind it, and the preview answers 500 for good. This is exactly the m10 'must not delete the only copy' state that the declared sweep deviation claims to protect. Make recoverSetAside report whether the set-aside file must be kept. Keep it when the restoring rename failed, or when the row lookup failed with anything other than sql.ErrNoRows. In the removal loop, skip those names so the next start can try again. [shown by a failing run] The engine ran the code review's test for this, internal/reports/sweep_restore_failure_test.go, with `go test -count=1 -run ^TestSweepKeepsASetAsideFileItCouldNotRestore$ ./internal/reports`, and it FAILED. Put that test at internal/reports/sweep_restore_failure_test.go as it is -- comments and layout aside -- and make it pass. The engine runs `go test -count=1 -run ^TestSweepKeepsASetAsideFileItCouldNotRestore$ ./internal/reports` again in your tree, and that run is what closes this; your word does not. The test: package reports import ( "bytes" "os" "path/filepath" "testing" ) // A crash while the canonical path is empty leaves the only copy of the bytes // the row describes in tmp/<id>.old. If the restart cannot put it back, it must // not delete it either. func TestSweepKeepsASetAsideFileItCouldNotRestore(t *testing.T) { r := newRig(t) v1 := htmlOf(300, "v1") rep := r.mustSave(goodForm("crash", "Crash", "published", v1)) old, cur := r.lib.setAsidePath(rep.ID), r.lib.path(rep.ID) // The replace set v1 aside and stopped: the row still says v1. if err := os.Rename(cur, old); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } // Something at the canonical path makes the restoring rename fail. if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(cur, "blocker"), 0o700); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } // Restart. Refusing to start is acceptable; deleting the only copy is not. _, _ = Open(Options{DB: r.st.DB(), DataDir: r.root, MaxUploadBytes: testCap, Now: r.clock.Now}) for _, p := range []string{old, cur} { if b, err := os.ReadFile(p); err == nil && bytes.Equal(b, v1) { return } } t.Fatal("the only copy of the report's bytes was deleted after the restore failed") }
